chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Buck's marriage and strain between them offstage
summary: The act stayed the same, but Buck, urged by his wife, resented Bubbles' advice on dress and conduct; Bubbles says Black people have trouble with each other.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: You talked a little bit about Buck getting married and your advice to him that he not get married -- in '26, you said?
What happened to your act? Did you go through any changes as a result of him getting married?

No, the act didn't go through any changes. The character of the people involved went through changes. The act still stayed the same. But off stage, between times, that's where the characters changed because I was trying to, as I said to you before, you see when I was trying to tell Buck things that I thought would be better for Buck and Bubbles as a whole amongst the public concerning his appearance, concerning his characterizations and all in the street and then amongst the public, he didn't want to believe that I knew to tell him. And then he'd relate to his

wife, I guess, and she telling him that I was trying to be better than him. I couldn't see it, so I let it go ahead. Then it come to a place where they knew more about the act than I did. It was mine, I created it. The point of it is I had difficulty with them. I had trouble with him because he believed everything the white man and didn't believe nothing the negro said and there was a reason for that, too, I guess.

Don't ask me. That's just his belief, okay? Just like the day we have more difficulty with our people than we do with the white people. That's the way it happens, because the negro has been trained to be opposite against each other in early, early years. It's hard to get that out of their blood, I guess. So that they're more selfish, they're jealous, they have the most -- oh, I can't begin to tell youhow our people are
in more walks of life than one. That's a story of its own, you know? And what can you do?
That seems to be a theme within your life, in a certain sense.
That you're always continually dealing with people like that.
That's right. It's a hard pill to swallow, but to have to swallow it anyway.
From the time you were a child.

I wouldn't say when you were a child because your mother comes between you and your parents come between you there and you have to deal with the parents then instead of the child. But we still have the same problem when you go to school with the principal and the parents of the children, you have the same trouble. But this hand to hand down, I don't
know why. I could go on endlessly talking about these different things, but what can you do? We won't get our story told.
